text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Doctors say they will fight against a proposed law to introduce hospital call duty only over weekends and holidays.
- Chamber of Economy says reducing Austria's ballooning wage costs could save firms as much as 17 billion schillings.
- Creditanstalt is to sell its stake in AVA-Bank.

- Province of Upper Austria said it will boycott Bank Austria, the country's biggest bank, following the closure of Austria Faserwerke this week. The plant was just recently sold by fibre maker Lenzing, in which the bank holds a major stake, to Germany's Hoechst.
- Construction group Strabag first-half pre-tax profit fell to 158.2 million schillings from 123.9 million last year, despite an increase in new orders.
- Mauerbach auction of Austrian Jewish artwork looted by Nazi Germany in World War Two exceeds all expectations.
- Austrian shop opening hours to be extended despite strong criticism by employers and trade unions. New law approved by the council of ministers on Wednesday.

- Listed Vienna Airport says it will take legal action against the government over its refusal to shoulder parts of a 375 million schilling investment required to make the airport fit for introduction of European Union's Schengen agreement.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank opened its sixth subsidiary in the Czech Republic.
- Italy's Benetton Group eyes acquisition of 13 Austrian motorway restaurants.
